sections.title: What Pharmacy First is
sections.proseHtml:
Pharmacy First is a community pharmacy pathway that lets a pharmacist assess eligible common conditions when symptoms fit the Pharmacy First pathway. Treatment is supplied only where pathway criteria are met; otherwise you receive advice or referral.

Pathway suitability is confirmed during consultation — not assumed from your postcode.

Pharmacy First is a community pharmacy pathway that lets a pharmacist assess eligible common conditions when symptoms fit the Pharmacy First pathway. Treatment is supplied only where pathway criteria are met; otherwise you receive advice or referral. The service is designed to give a clear outcome in one visit: treatment where appropriate, practical self-care guidance, or a safe referral when pharmacy care is not enough. Patients from your area can call ahead to confirm whether a consultation is available before travelling.

sections.title: Eligibility and suitability
sections.proseHtml:
Conditions Pharmacy First May Cover

Pharmacy First covers defined pathway conditions. The pharmacist confirms what can be assessed for you on the day.

  • Pharmacist assessment
  • Clear next-step advice
  • Safety-netting
  • Urgent-care guidance when needed

sections.title: What happens during the consultation
sections.proseHtml:
1. What Happens During The Consultation Your visit follows a structured consultation so decisions are clinically safe and clearly explained. You will be asked about when symptoms started, what you have already tried, and which medicines you take. The pharmacist explains what can be managed under the pathway and what falls outside it. Where treatment is suitable, you leave with clear instructions; where it is not, you leave with next-step advice rather than uncertainty. Bring a medicines list if you can, and mention allergies, pregnancy or breastfeeding early in the conversation. If you need to check how the service is arranged availability or booking options first, call . Pharmacist assessment Clear next-step advice
  2. What Happens During The Consultation The consultation is a private, structured conversation shaped around your symptoms and day-to-day context in your area. You will cover what has already been tried, current medicines and whether pharmacy treatment is clinically suitable. If treatment is appropriate, dosing and safety advice are explained clearly. If it is not, the pharmacist still gives practical guidance on GP, NHS 111 or urgent care. Telephone if you need to check consultation availability around family or work schedules. Pharmacist assessment Clear next-step advice
  3. What Happens During The Consultation The visit is designed to be efficient: gather the key clinical facts, decide the safest outcome, and explain what to do next. Have a medicines list ready and note when symptoms started so the review moves quickly. You may receive treatment where pathway criteria are met, or advice and referral where they are not. That clarity is the point of the consultation for busy patients travelling from your area. Call if you want to check how the service is arranged or booking options first. Pharmacist assessment Clear next-step advice
  4. What Happens During The Consultation When you arrive from your area, the consultation is kept focused so the journey is worthwhile. Expect questions about symptom timing, medicines already tried, allergies and any red-flag concerns. The pharmacist then explains what sits inside the pathway and what needs medical care instead. You leave with instructions for treatment, self-care or referral — not with an ambiguous next step. Call beforehand if you want to confirm what to bring. Pharmacist assessment Clear next-step advice

sections.title: What To Bring
sections.proseHtml:
What To Bring

Have a medicines list ready and note when symptoms started, what you have already tried, and any allergies.

  • Medicines list
  • Symptom timeline
  • Allergy information
  • Questions for the pharmacist

sections.title: When To Contact A GP, NHS 111 Or Emergency Services
sections.proseHtml: When To Contact A GP, NHS 111 Or Emergency Services Contact your GP, NHS 111, or urgent care if symptoms are persistent beyond expected recovery, keep worsening despite pharmacy advice, or suggest a more serious infection. Seek urgent medical care for breathing difficulties, chest pain, severe dehydration, confusion, a non-blanching rash, or any emergency symptoms that make you feel critically unwell. Pharmacy pathways are for defined minor illnesses only — if you are pregnant, caring for a very young child outside pathway age limits, or already under active GP review for the same problem, arrange medical assessment instead. If you are unsure after symptoms start in your area, call before travelling and ask whether a Pharmacy First consultation is appropriate today. Pharmacist assessment Clear next-step advice Safety-netting Urgent-care guidance when needed

processSteps.title: Contact the pharmacy
processSteps.body: Contact the pharmacy to confirm how Pharmacy First is currently arranged. The pharmacy team will ask appropriate questions about your symptoms and medicines. Suitability and next steps are determined individually.

processSteps.title: A structured conversation
processSteps.body: The conversation is shaped around your symptoms and day-to-day context in your area. The team will ask what you have already tried and which medicines you take. Where the service is not appropriate, you will be advised where to seek further help.

processSteps.title: Share a medicines list
processSteps.body: Have a medicines list ready and note when symptoms started so the conversation is clear. The pharmacy team will ask appropriate questions. Suitability and next steps are determined individually.

processSteps.title: Questions about timing and medicines
processSteps.body: When you contact the pharmacy from your area, expect questions about symptom timing, medicines already tried, allergies and any warning signs. The team then explains whether Pharmacy First may be suitable. If it is not, you will be advised where to seek further help.

faqs.question: Can your area patients use Pharmacy First?
faqs.answer: That depends on your symptoms and Pharmacy First pathway criteria. The pharmacist confirms suitability during consultation — contact the pharmacy on .

faqs.question: What should I bring to Pharmacy First from your area?
faqs.answer: Bring your medicines list, describe when symptoms started, and mention allergies, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Call beforehand if you are unsure whether a consultation is appropriate.

faqs.question: What if Pharmacy First is not suitable for my symptoms?
faqs.answer: The pharmacist will explain when to use your GP, NHS 111, or urgent care instead, so you leave with a clear plan.

faqs.question: Is Pharmacy First part of everyday care for your area residents?
faqs.answer: It can be a practical first step for eligible common conditions, with treatment, advice or referral explained during consultation. Contact the pharmacy on .

faqs.question: What should I bring from your area?
faqs.answer: Bring a medicines list, note when symptoms started, and mention allergies, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Call if you are unsure whether to attend.

faqs.question: Can families in your area use Pharmacy First?
faqs.answer: Some pathways include age limits. The pharmacist confirms suitability for children during consultation — call if you want to check first.

faqs.question: Can I check suitability quickly from your area?
faqs.answer: Yes. Call and describe your symptoms before rearranging your day.

faqs.question: What should I bring to keep the visit efficient?
faqs.answer: Bring your medicines list and be ready to explain when symptoms started, what you have tried, and any allergies.
